title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Tioga, ND, site of North Dakota's first oil well? Deep production history plus modern Bakken drilling. Get an honest offer.
heroLead: North Dakota's first commercial oil well came in near Tioga back in April of 1951, decades before the Bakken boom, and that history still shapes what mineral ownership looks like here today.
intro: The Clarence Iverson #1 proved oil could be produced in this part of the state long before horizontal drilling made the Bakken shale itself economical, and Tioga has carried an oil-town identity for generations because of it. Families who've held mineral rights here since before the modern boom sometimes have older leases layered under newer horizontal wells on the very same tract.

sections.heading: Seventy years of oil history on one tract
paragraphs: It's not unusual for a Tioga-area mineral interest to have an original 1950s-era conventional lease, followed decades later by a modern Bakken horizontal well on the same or an adjacent spacing unit. Sorting out which lease actually governs your interest today, and whether the older one properly terminated, is real title work we do before making an offer.

sections.heading: Tioga's place in the modern Bakken core
paragraphs: Beyond its history, Tioga sits within genuinely strong modern Bakken acreage, with continued horizontal development over the past fifteen-plus years. We check both the historical and current well records tied to your legal description so nothing gets missed.

sections.heading: A family legacy that outlasted the first boom
paragraphs: Some Tioga families have now watched two distinct oil eras play out on the same ground, the original 1950s conventional wells their grandparents leased, and the modern horizontal wells that came decades later. Each generation has had a different relationship to that mineral interest, from curiosity to real income to eventual decisions about whether to keep or sell.
We treat that layered history with the attention it deserves, confirming exactly which leases and wells apply to your interest today before we ever discuss a number.

faqs.question: Our family has a lease dating back to the 1950s. Is that still relevant?
faqs.answer: Possibly. We check whether older Tioga-area leases were properly released or if they still affect current ownership before making an offer.

faqs.question: Is Tioga still an active part of the Bakken today?
faqs.answer: Yes, this area has seen substantial modern horizontal development in addition to its older conventional history.

faqs.question: How do you handle a tract with both old and new wells?
faqs.answer: We research the complete well history for your specific legal description and explain how each well, old or new, factors into your interest's value.

faqs.question: Does the historical significance of Tioga's first well affect what our minerals are worth today?
faqs.answer: Not directly, value comes from current production and remaining reserves, not history. But the historical layer does affect title work, which we check carefully.
